slides.say: So a kite has two pairs of equal sides. In each pair, the equal sides sit next to each other, not facing each other. In this kite, the two pairs have different lengths. They can also be equal, and then it's a rhombus.

A kite is symmetric along the line that joins the two corners between equal sides, here A and C. If we fold along A C, the left half lands exactly on the right half. That works even when the kite is turned on the page.

The diagonals of a kite are not necessarily equal. We give them names, the main diagonal and the secondary diagonal.
The main diagonal is the kite's line of symmetry. It joins the two corners that sit between equal sides, here A and C. It cuts the kite into two triangles, left and right, that are exactly the same.
The secondary diagonal, from B to D, does not necessarily cut the kite into two equal parts. In this kite, the triangle on top and the triangle at the bottom are different.
The diagonals of a kite are perpendicular to each other. And the main diagonal cuts the secondary one into two equal halves.
